title: Keep the Beat
strapline: Bounce, clap, tap and drum — feeling a steady pulse in your body from the very first months.
intent: Babies and young children feel and respond to a steady beat with their whole bodies — bouncing, swaying, clapping.
Children develop rhythm, timing and coordination through moving to a pulse.
Children join in with songs, rhymes and drumming, anticipating the beat and the good bits.
Children explore fast and slow, loud and quiet, and beats they make themselves.
Children build the early rhythmic awareness that underpins language, phonics and music.
implementation: Bounce babies gently on your knee to a steady beat, and sway and rock young ones to the pulse of a song.
Sing the same rhythmic rhymes daily so children anticipate the beat and join in with body and voice.
Provide drums, pots and shakers and tap a steady beat for children to copy and feel.
Play with the beat — speed it up, slow it down, make it loud then a whisper — and watch them respond.
Clap and pat names and words — 'Ay-la', 'ba-na-na' — feeling the syllables as beats.
Follow the children's own beats: when a baby bangs a pot on purpose, echo it back with delight.
Keep it joyful and physical — the beat is felt in the body long before it's understood.
key_questions: (For babies, wonder aloud) You're bouncing right along with the song, aren't you?
Can you tap the drum just like me — tap, tap, tap?
Shall we go faster now... or really, really slow?
Can you feel the beat in your feet?
You made that sound on purpose — shall we do it again?

impact.text: Babies respond to music with their whole bodies — stilling, bouncing, swaying, vocalising.
Children make sounds on purpose and enjoy the effect, banging, shaking and tapping.
Children join in favourite songs and rhymes with actions and anticipate the good bits.
Children copy a steady beat and explore fast and slow, loud and quiet.
Children feel syllables as beats when names and words are clapped and patted.
Children copy simple actions in songs and games — clap, wave, pat.

enhancements: Drums, pots, pans and shakers for tapping a beat.
A basket of well-loved bouncing and action rhymes.
Ribbons and scarves for swaying and moving to the pulse.
Music of different tempos to speed up and slow down to.
A low mirror so babies see themselves moving to the beat.
Name cards for clapping out the syllables in children's names.
A soft space for lap-bouncing and rocking with the littlest ones.

playing_exploring: Babies explore sound and rhythm with their whole bodies and voices.
They test banging, shaking and tapping to hear what each makes.
active_learning: Children ask for favourite rhymes again and again, feeling the beat each time.
A baby returns to a pot they can drum, delighting in the sound they control.
creating_thinking: Children make sounds and beats on purpose and repeat what works.
They begin to anticipate the beat and the actions that go with it.
